$comment: GENERATED by tools/rules-engine from rules/base.rules.yaml and every **/module.rules.yaml. Do not edit.

required.statement: Controllers and endpoints only bind input, call one Application use case and map the result; no business logic, no data access.
Application code depends only on Domain types and ports (interfaces); it never references EF Core, DbContext or infrastructure types.
A module references another module only when listed in its mayDependOn, and never one listed in mustNotDependOn.
Every endpoint has a permission attribute, takes and returns PublicId (never raw database ids), validates its input with a validator and returns errors as problem+json.
Lookup and reference data is created and changed only through EF migrations, never by runtime seeders or manual SQL.

Changes to rules/, packages/, .claude/, the exemptions of any module.rules.yaml, deploy/, .github/, docs/adr/, provenance/, tools/extract/, tools/build.ps1 and the repo-wide build settings need platform-owner review.
Enums are stored and sent as integers and every enum member has an explicit numeric value (Approved = 3), so reordering never changes stored data; labels come from i18n, never from enum names.

Status ids, role keys, permission keys, error codes, config keys, claim types, route names, cache keys, job ids and limits live in typed constants or options classes; numeric literals other than the allowed ones need a named constant.

Use named arguments for non-obvious parameters, small single-purpose methods, guard clauses instead of nesting, meaningful names, and no dead or commented-out code; size and complexity stay within the module thresholds.
Every Application use case, validator, workflow transition, domain rule and Angular service or component with logic ships with unit tests, and each module meets its line-coverage threshold.
Screens are built only from @codelab/ng-dga components and the 8 page patterns.
No user-visible raw text in templates or components; every string is an i18n key present in both ar and en.
Styles use design tokens (CSS variables) and logical properties (inline-start/end) so RTL and LTR both work.
Every route and every action button is gated by a typed permission key.

forbidden.description: Reading the system clock directly makes time untestable.
forbidden.fix: Inject TimeProvider and call GetUtcNow() (or GetLocalNow() for display); tests use FakeTimeProvider.

forbidden.description: Thread.Sleep blocks a thread and makes waits untestable; it is also a global banned API (RS0030) in Codelab.Build.Sdk.
forbidden.fix: Use await Task.Delay(delay, timeProvider, cancellationToken) so waits are async and testable.

forbidden.description: Turning off the banned-API, complexity or clean-code (CLB) analyzers removes a build gate for everyone after you (a gate switch set to anything but true, the .NET analyzers or the analysis level off, by id, by a bare pragma, by category severity, by marking code generated, or by relaxing warnings-as-errors). Codelab.Build.Sdk also fails the build (CODELAB002, CODELAB003).
forbidden.fix: Fix the code instead. A justified exception is a module.rules.yaml exemption with a reason, reviewed by the platform owner.

forbidden.description: CodelabFixtureGateOptOut lets a build switch the quality gates off without CODELAB002; only the SDK's own fixture builds may pass it.
forbidden.fix: Remove it. The quality gates stay on for every project; fix the code instead.

forbidden.description: Roslyn loads any .globalconfig it is given, at any global_level, so a hand-written one can raise the clean-code thresholds or switch rules off for a whole project; the only one is the generated rules/codelab.globalconfig.
forbidden.fix: Delete the file. Change thresholds in rules/base.rules.yaml or a module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: An auto-generated header makes every analyzer skip the file (CLB1001-CLB1005 ignore generated code), so hand-written code must not carry one.
forbidden.fix: Remove the header. Real generator output is written under obj/ by the build and is never committed.

forbidden.description: A *.g.cs, *.generated.cs or *.designer.cs name makes the analyzers treat a hand-written file as generated and skip it.
forbidden.fix: Rename the file to a plain *.cs name. Generator output lives under obj/ and is never committed.

forbidden.description: Only a *.Tests project is a test project (CLB1004 magic numbers skips test projects). Production code may not declare IsTestProject, reference a test framework (Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk sets IsTestProject) or rename its assembly to *.Tests.
forbidden.fix: Put tests in a project named <Module>.Tests; production code never declares IsTestProject.

forbidden.description: A certificate validator that accepts everything turns TLS into plain text for an attacker in the path (the harvest source's internal calls did this).
forbidden.fix: Keep certificate validation on. Trust an internal CA through Codelab.Integration's ServerCertificatePolicy (pinned or chain-validated), never by returning true.

forbidden.description: Clean-code thresholds (codelab_* keys) written by hand bypass the rules files and their review; only the files the rules engine emits, at their own paths (rules/codelab.globalconfig and each module's .editorconfig), may set them. A GENERATED marker in the content proves nothing.
forbidden.fix: Change the thresholds or settings in rules/base.rules.yaml or the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: Permission keys passed as string literals drift from the permission catalog.
forbidden.fix: Use the typed permission constant (Permissions.<Area>.<Action> in C#, PermissionKeys.<KEY> in TypeScript).

forbidden.description: Role checks with string literals bypass the permission model.
forbidden.fix: Check a permission with [HasPermission(Permissions.<Area>.<Action>)] instead of a role name.

forbidden.description: Configuration read by string key is untyped and unvalidated.
forbidden.fix: Bind a typed options class with a SectionName constant and ValidateOnStart, then inject IOptions<T>.

forbidden.description: Enums stored or serialized as strings break when a member is renamed.
forbidden.fix: Keep the EF default (int column) and the numeric JSON value; the client maps numbers to i18n labels with the generated TS enum.

forbidden.description: An enum member without an explicit value changes meaning when members are reordered (CLB1005 is the build gate).
forbidden.fix: Give every enum member an explicit numeric value, e.g. Draft = 1, Submitted = 2.

forbidden.description: The Api layer must not touch the database directly.
forbidden.fix: Call an Application use case; only the composition root registers the DbContext.

forbidden.description: Application code must depend on ports, not on EF Core.
forbidden.fix: Declare a port (repository or IUnitOfWork interface) in Application and implement it in Infrastructure.

forbidden.description: Raw numeric or Guid database ids in routes leak internal keys.
forbidden.fix: Take a PublicId route value ({id}) and resolve it in the Application layer.

forbidden.description: An empty catch block hides failures.
forbidden.fix: Handle the error, or let it reach the global exception handler; log with the reference code when you rethrow.

forbidden.description: Commented-out code is dead code; git keeps the history.
forbidden.fix: Delete the commented-out code.

forbidden.description: Feature code must not call HTTP directly.
forbidden.fix: Inject ApiService (or the generated API client) from core/api; it owns the base URL, auth and signing headers.

forbidden.description: Route and API paths typed as literals drift from the route and API catalogs.
forbidden.fix: Use the typed route constants (AppRoutes) and the generated API client instead of path literals.

forbidden.description: Third-party UI kits and external DGA packages are not allowed (D5).
forbidden.fix: Use the matching component from @codelab/ng-dga, or ask the platform owner to add one.

forbidden.description: Raw text in a template is not translated.
forbidden.fix: Add ar and en keys to the i18n files and use {{ 'feature.key' | translate }}.

forbidden.description: Physical left/right properties break RTL.
forbidden.fix: Use logical properties (margin-inline-start, inset-inline-end, text-align start/end).

forbidden.description: Raw colours bypass the design tokens.
forbidden.fix: Use a design token, e.g. var(--codelab-color-primary).

modules.description: Clean-code Roslyn analyzers CLB1001-CLB1005 shipped inside Codelab.Build.Sdk; thresholds from the generated module .editorconfig, then rules/codelab.globalconfig.

forbidden.description: An enum member without an explicit value changes meaning when members are reordered (CLB1005 is the build gate).
forbidden.fix: Give every enum member an explicit numeric value, e.g. Draft = 1, Submitted = 2.

forbidden.description: The Api layer must not touch the database directly.
forbidden.fix: Call an Application use case; only the composition root registers the DbContext.

forbidden.description: Application code must depend on ports, not on EF Core.
forbidden.fix: Declare a port (repository or IUnitOfWork interface) in Application and implement it in Infrastructure.

forbidden.description: Raw numeric or Guid database ids in routes leak internal keys.
forbidden.fix: Take a PublicId route value ({id}) and resolve it in the Application layer.

forbidden.description: An empty catch block hides failures.
forbidden.fix: Handle the error, or let it reach the global exception handler; log with the reference code when you rethrow.

forbidden.description: Commented-out code is dead code; git keeps the history.
forbidden.fix: Delete the commented-out code.

forbidden.description: Feature code must not call HTTP directly.
forbidden.fix: Inject ApiService (or the generated API client) from core/api; it owns the base URL, auth and signing headers.

forbidden.description: Route and API paths typed as literals drift from the route and API catalogs.
forbidden.fix: Use the typed route constants (AppRoutes) and the generated API client instead of path literals.

forbidden.description: Third-party UI kits and external DGA packages are not allowed (D5).
forbidden.fix: Use the matching component from @codelab/ng-dga, or ask the platform owner to add one.

forbidden.description: Raw text in a template is not translated.
forbidden.fix: Add ar and en keys to the i18n files and use {{ 'feature.key' | translate }}.

forbidden.description: Physical left/right properties break RTL.
forbidden.fix: Use logical properties (margin-inline-start, inset-inline-end, text-align start/end).

forbidden.description: Raw colours bypass the design tokens.
forbidden.fix: Use a design token, e.g. var(--codelab-color-primary).

modules.description: Serilog + OpenTelemetry + Seq host bootstrap, correlation, reference codes, PII masking, user hash, job failure log filter, health endpoints.

required.statement: Controllers and endpoints only bind input, call one Application use case and map the result; no business logic, no data access.
Application code depends only on Domain types and ports (interfaces); it never references EF Core, DbContext or infrastructure types.
A module references another module only when listed in its mayDependOn, and never one listed in mustNotDependOn.
Every endpoint has a permission attribute, takes and returns PublicId (never raw database ids), validates its input with a validator and returns errors as problem+json.
Lookup and reference data is created and changed only through EF migrations, never by runtime seeders or manual SQL.

Changes to rules/, packages/, .claude/, the exemptions of any module.rules.yaml, deploy/, .github/, docs/adr/, provenance/, tools/extract/, tools/build.ps1 and the repo-wide build settings need platform-owner review.
Enums are stored and sent as integers and every enum member has an explicit numeric value (Approved = 3), so reordering never changes stored data; labels come from i18n, never from enum names.

Status ids, role keys, permission keys, error codes, config keys, claim types, route names, cache keys, job ids and limits live in typed constants or options classes; numeric literals other than the allowed ones need a named constant.

Use named arguments for non-obvious parameters, small single-purpose methods, guard clauses instead of nesting, meaningful names, and no dead or commented-out code; size and complexity stay within the module thresholds.
Every Application use case, validator, workflow transition, domain rule and Angular service or component with logic ships with unit tests, and each module meets its line-coverage threshold.
Screens are built only from @codelab/ng-dga components and the 8 page patterns.
No user-visible raw text in templates or components; every string is an i18n key present in both ar and en.
Styles use design tokens (CSS variables) and logical properties (inline-start/end) so RTL and LTR both work.
Every route and every action button is gated by a typed permission key.

forbidden.description: Reading the system clock directly makes time untestable.
forbidden.fix: Inject TimeProvider and call GetUtcNow() (or GetLocalNow() for display); tests use FakeTimeProvider.

forbidden.description: Thread.Sleep blocks a thread and makes waits untestable; it is also a global banned API (RS0030) in Codelab.Build.Sdk.
forbidden.fix: Use await Task.Delay(delay, timeProvider, cancellationToken) so waits are async and testable.

forbidden.description: Turning off the banned-API, complexity or clean-code (CLB) analyzers removes a build gate for everyone after you (a gate switch set to anything but true, the .NET analyzers or the analysis level off, by id, by a bare pragma, by category severity, by marking code generated, or by relaxing warnings-as-errors). Codelab.Build.Sdk also fails the build (CODELAB002, CODELAB003).
forbidden.fix: Fix the code instead. A justified exception is a module.rules.yaml exemption with a reason, reviewed by the platform owner.

forbidden.description: CodelabFixtureGateOptOut lets a build switch the quality gates off without CODELAB002; only the SDK's own fixture builds may pass it.
forbidden.fix: Remove it. The quality gates stay on for every project; fix the code instead.

forbidden.description: Roslyn loads any .globalconfig it is given, at any global_level, so a hand-written one can raise the clean-code thresholds or switch rules off for a whole project; the only one is the generated rules/codelab.globalconfig.
forbidden.fix: Delete the file. Change thresholds in rules/base.rules.yaml or a module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: An auto-generated header makes every analyzer skip the file (CLB1001-CLB1005 ignore generated code), so hand-written code must not carry one.
forbidden.fix: Remove the header. Real generator output is written under obj/ by the build and is never committed.

forbidden.description: A *.g.cs, *.generated.cs or *.designer.cs name makes the analyzers treat a hand-written file as generated and skip it.
forbidden.fix: Rename the file to a plain *.cs name. Generator output lives under obj/ and is never committed.

forbidden.description: Only a *.Tests project is a test project (CLB1004 magic numbers skips test projects). Production code may not declare IsTestProject, reference a test framework (Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk sets IsTestProject) or rename its assembly to *.Tests.
forbidden.fix: Put tests in a project named <Module>.Tests; production code never declares IsTestProject.

forbidden.description: A certificate validator that accepts everything turns TLS into plain text for an attacker in the path (the harvest source's internal calls did this).
forbidden.fix: Keep certificate validation on. Trust an internal CA through Codelab.Integration's ServerCertificatePolicy (pinned or chain-validated), never by returning true.

forbidden.description: Clean-code thresholds (codelab_* keys) written by hand bypass the rules files and their review; only the files the rules engine emits, at their own paths (rules/codelab.globalconfig and each module's .editorconfig), may set them. A GENERATED marker in the content proves nothing.
forbidden.fix: Change the thresholds or settings in rules/base.rules.yaml or the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: An auto-generated header makes every analyzer skip the file (CLB1001-CLB1005 ignore generated code), so hand-written code must not carry one.
forbidden.fix: Remove the header. Real generator output is written under obj/ by the build and is never committed.

forbidden.description: A *.g.cs, *.generated.cs or *.designer.cs name makes the analyzers treat a hand-written file as generated and skip it.
forbidden.fix: Rename the file to a plain *.cs name. Generator output lives under obj/ and is never committed.

forbidden.description: Only a *.Tests project is a test project (CLB1004 magic numbers skips test projects). Production code may not declare IsTestProject, reference a test framework (Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk sets IsTestProject) or rename its assembly to *.Tests.
forbidden.fix: Put tests in a project named <Module>.Tests; production code never declares IsTestProject.

forbidden.description: A certificate validator that accepts everything turns TLS into plain text for an attacker in the path (the harvest source's internal calls did this).
forbidden.fix: Keep certificate validation on. Trust an internal CA through Codelab.Integration's ServerCertificatePolicy (pinned or chain-validated), never by returning true.

forbidden.description: Clean-code thresholds (codelab_* keys) written by hand bypass the rules files and their review; only the files the rules engine emits, at their own paths (rules/codelab.globalconfig and each module's .editorconfig), may set them. A GENERATED marker in the content proves nothing.
forbidden.fix: Change the thresholds or settings in rules/base.rules.yaml or the module.rules.yaml, then run node tools/rules-engine/compile.mjs.

forbidden.description: Permission keys passed as string literals drift from the permission catalog.
forbidden.fix: Use the typed permission constant (Permissions.<Area>.<Action> in C#, PermissionKeys.<KEY> in TypeScript).

forbidden.description: Role checks with string literals bypass the permission model.
forbidden.fix: Check a permission with [HasPermission(Permissions.<Area>.<Action>)] instead of a role name.

forbidden.description: Configuration read by string key is untyped and unvalidated.
forbidden.fix: Bind a typed options class with a SectionName constant and ValidateOnStart, then inject IOptions<T>.

forbidden.description: Enums stored or serialized as strings break when a member is renamed.
forbidden.fix: Keep the EF default (int column) and the numeric JSON value; the client maps numbers to i18n labels with the generated TS enum.

forbidden.description: An enum member without an explicit value changes meaning when members are reordered (CLB1005 is the build gate).
forbidden.fix: Give every enum member an explicit numeric value, e.g. Draft = 1, Submitted = 2.

forbidden.description: The Api layer must not touch the database directly.
forbidden.fix: Call an Application use case; only the composition root registers the DbContext.

forbidden.description: Application code must depend on ports, not on EF Core.
forbidden.fix: Declare a port (repository or IUnitOfWork interface) in Application and implement it in Infrastructure.

forbidden.description: Raw numeric or Guid database ids in routes leak internal keys.
forbidden.fix: Take a PublicId route value ({id}) and resolve it in the Application layer.

forbidden.description: An empty catch block hides failures.
forbidden.fix: Handle the error, or let it reach the global exception handler; log with the reference code when you rethrow.

forbidden.description: Commented-out code is dead code; git keeps the history.
forbidden.fix: Delete the commented-out code.

forbidden.description: Feature code must not call HTTP directly.
forbidden.fix: Inject ApiService (or the generated API client) from core/api; it owns the base URL, auth and signing headers.

forbidden.description: Route and API paths typed as literals drift from the route and API catalogs.
forbidden.fix: Use the typed route constants (AppRoutes) and the generated API client instead of path literals.

forbidden.description: Third-party UI kits and external DGA packages are not allowed (D5).
forbidden.fix: Use the matching component from @codelab/ng-dga, or ask the platform owner to add one.

forbidden.description: Raw text in a template is not translated.
forbidden.fix: Add ar and en keys to the i18n files and use {{ 'feature.key' | translate }}.

forbidden.description: Physical left/right properties break RTL.
forbidden.fix: Use logical properties (margin-inline-start, inset-inline-end, text-align start/end).

forbidden.description: Raw colours bypass the design tokens.
forbidden.fix: Use a design token, e.g. var(--codelab-color-primary).

modules.description: Frontend tooling: ESLint boundary preset, codelab/wire-id-cast, Stylelint preset, codelab-vectors-sync.

required.statement: Controllers and endpoints only bind input, call one Application use case and map the result; no business logic, no data access.
Application code depends only on Domain types and ports (interfaces); it never references EF Core, DbContext or infrastructure types.
A module references another module only when listed in its mayDependOn, and never one listed in mustNotDependOn.
Every endpoint has a permission attribute, takes and returns PublicId (never raw database ids), validates its input with a validator and returns errors as problem+json.
Lookup and reference data is created and changed only through EF migrations, never by runtime seeders or manual SQL.

Changes to rules/, packages/, .claude/, the exemptions of any module.rules.yaml, deploy/, .github/, docs/adr/, provenance/, tools/extract/, tools/build.ps1 and the repo-wide build settings need platform-owner review.
Enums are stored and sent as integers and every enum member has an explicit numeric value (Approved = 3), so reordering never changes stored data; labels come from i18n, never from enum names.

Status ids, role keys, permission keys, error codes, config keys, claim types, route names, cache keys, job ids and limits live in typed constants or options classes; numeric literals other than the allowed ones need a named constant.

Use named arguments for non-obvious parameters, small single-purpose methods, guard clauses instead of nesting, meaningful names, and no dead or commented-out code; size and complexity stay within the module thresholds.
Every Application use case, validator, workflow transition, domain rule and Angular service or component with logic ships with unit tests, and each module meets its line-coverage threshold.
Screens are built only from @codelab/ng-dga components and the 8 page patterns.
No user-visible raw text in templates or components; every string is an i18n key present in both ar and en.
Styles use design tokens (CSS variables) and logical properties (inline-start/end) so RTL and LTR both work.
Every route and every action button is gated by a typed permission key.

forbidden.description: Reading the system clock directly makes time untestable.
forbidden.fix: Inject TimeProvider and call GetUtcNow() (or GetLocalNow() for display); tests use FakeTimeProvider.

forbidden.description: Thread.Sleep blocks a thread and makes waits untestable; it is also a global banned API (RS0030) in Codelab.Build.Sdk.
forbidden.fix: Use await Task.Delay(delay, timeProvider, cancellationToken) so waits are async and testable.

forbidden.description: Turning off the banned-API, complexity or clean-code (CLB) analyzers removes a build gate for everyone after you (a gate switch set to anything but true, the .NET analyzers or the analysis level off, by id, by a bare pragma, by category severity, by marking code generated, or by relaxing warnings-as-errors). Codelab.Build.Sdk also fails the build (CODELAB002, CODELAB003).
forbidden.fix: Fix the code instead. A justified exception is a module.rules.yaml exemption with a reason, reviewed by the platform owner.

forbidden.description: CodelabFixtureGateOptOut lets a build switch the quality gates off without CODELAB002; only the SDK's own fixture builds may pass it.
forbidden.fix: Remove it. The quality gates stay on for every project; fix the code instead.
